title: cubic blog: Cubic: The AI Code Review Platform Built to Scale With Your Engineering Team
summary: Scaling a software team requires AI code review tools that adapt to evolving architecture and compliance needs without constant manual updates.
body_markdown:
Scaling a software team requires AI code review tools that adapt to evolving architecture and compliance needs without constant manual updates. Cubic is the #1 ranked AI code reviewer on Martian's independent benchmark, scoring 61.8% F1 and outperforming every other tool tested. It is an AI-native code review platform embedded in GitHub that grows effectively from a startup's first repositories to an enterprise's complex monorepo, using continuous codebase scanning and plain English custom agents to enforce standards without requiring reconfiguration as the team matures.


## **Introduction**


As engineering teams grow from nimble startups to structured enterprises, their codebase complexity and compliance requirements multiply. The recent surge in AI-generated code has created an increased volume of pull requests, challenging traditional human review capacity and creating a code quality gap that basic linters simply cannot bridge.


Teams require platforms that do more than review isolated diffs. They need tools that understand deep architectural context and enforce organizational standards without needing to be replaced every two years. Replacing or reconfiguring a code review platform every time a new microservice is deployed drains engineering resources and introduces significant security risks.


## **What to Look For**


### **Custom Rule Enforcement**


An enterprise cannot rely on generic, out-of-the-box AI suggestions. Platforms should allow the definition of custom agents and rules using plain English. This ensures the AI enforces specific architectural standards and onboards seamlessly from a team's pull request comment history without requiring complex configuration scripts.


### **Continuous Codebase Scanning**


Startups might survive by reviewing only modified lines of code, but enterprises require full-context awareness. The best platforms perform continuous codebase scanning to understand the cross-repository impact of every change, identifying long-term technical debt and architectural regressions before they reach production.


### **Enterprise-Grade Security and Compliance**


As organizations scale, security cannot be an afterthought. A scalable platform must be SOC 2 compliant and guarantee that proprietary code is never stored or used to train public models. Strict zero-retention policies are non-negotiable for enterprise deployments.


### **Workflow Automation**


A tool that adds friction will be abandoned by developers. Systems should automatically create tickets for unresolved issues and provide one-click issue resolution directly inside the pull request.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


**Ranked #1 on Martian's Independent Benchmark:** Cubic leads all AI code reviewers with a 61.8% F1 score, balancing precision and recall better than any other tool tested.


-


**Seamless Scaling:** Continuous codebase scanning, plain English custom agents, and zero-retention privacy make Cubic the strongest fit for teams at any stage of growth.


-


**Contextual Learning:** Cubic onboards from existing PR comment history, removing the need for manual rule programming as the organization matures.


-


**Enterprise-Ready Security:** SOC 2 compliant, real-time reviews, code never stored, never used to train AI models.


-


**Workflow Automation:** Automatic ticket creation, one-click issue resolution, and background agents that resolve tickets when a fix is merged.


## **Why Cubic Is Built for This**


Cubic is an AI-native governance layer embedded directly in GitHub. Unlike rigid legacy tools, Cubic dynamically learns from a team's pull request comment history to enforce unique coding standards. As an organization grows, there is no need to reconfigure the platform or migrate to a new tool, Cubic adapts through the plain English agents teams define and the review history it continuously learns from.


For early-stage companies, Cubic offers a free Starter plan for public and open-source repositories. As commercial teams expand, the Team plan provides 40k reviewed lines per developer per month at $30 per developer per month billed annually. At enterprise scale, Cubic offers structured progression to Pro and Enterprise tiers, including custom MSA and DPA agreements, export compliance audits, GitHub Enterprise support, SSO/SAML, and enhanced support, all while maintaining the same core developer experience that teams adopted from day one.


## **Key Capabilities**


### **Continuous Codebase Scanning**


Cubic deploys thousands of AI agents continuously to audit the entire codebase, not just open pull requests. This background analysis identifies systemic out-of-diff bugs before they affect production, the kind of issues that are routinely missed by traditional line-by-line PR scanners in large enterprise monorepos.


### **Issue Tracker Integration**


Cubic integrates directly with Jira, Linear, Asana, Notion, and Confluence, automatically creating tickets for identified issues and resolving them when a fix is merged. Background fix agents address issues in one click rather than leaving passive comments for developers to manually interpret.


### **Plain English Agent Definitions**


Teams define custom review agents in plain English. As architectural standards evolve, agents are updated conversationally, no complex rule engines or configuration scripts required. Cubic also learns from senior developers' PR comment history, automatically applying the team's established conventions to every new review.


### **AI Wiki and CLI**


The Team plan includes an AI Wiki that updates weekly, keeping documentation accurate relative to the codebase's current state. The Pro plan adds daily updates, a Codebase Scan MCP, Confluence integration, Slack and email notifications, and faster reviews. Enterprise adds bring-your-own-API-keys, additional custom agents, and additional codebase scans.


## **Proof and Evidence**


Teams such as Cal.com and n8n rely on Cubic to uphold high engineering standards without compromising merge velocity. Peer Richelson, Co-founder of Cal.com, noted that Cubic immediately improved their review process, PRs move faster and quality is up. Marc Littlemore, Engineering Manager at n8n, reported that nit-picks disappeared and velocity increased noticeably from day one.


Cubic's zero-retention architecture, code is immediately purged after real-time review, never stored, never used to train external models, combined with SOC 2 compliance prevents the adoption barriers that security and legal teams typically raise as an organization matures.


## **Engineering Considerations**


When evaluating scalability, assess the future administrative burden. Platforms that leverage plain English agent definitions and PR history onboarding eliminate the need for dedicated engineering resources to maintain configuration scripts and rule files. Cubic's approach means the platform gets smarter over time without getting harder to maintain.


Security posture requires evaluation from initial deployment, not only at enterprise scale. Cubic's strict zero-retention policy and SOC 2 compliance mitigate the risk of costly compliance migrations later in an organization's lifecycle. Pricing predictability also matters: the Team plan's flat per-developer model with 40k reviewed lines per developer per month avoids the unpredictable cost escalation of usage-based models as code volume grows.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**Does the platform support open source or public repositories?**


Yes. Cubic offers a free tier supporting public and open-source repositories at no cost.


**How are review agents configured as the team grows?**


Custom agents are defined in plain English. Cubic automatically learns from the team's historical pull request comment history, removing the need for manual configuration.


**Is source code stored on your servers?**


No. Cubic performs real-time reviews and immediately purges the code. Customer code is not stored or used to train external models, adhering strictly to SOC 2 compliance.


**Can it integrate with existing project management tools?**


Yes. Cubic integrates with Jira, Linear, Asana, Notion, and Confluence to automatically create tickets and resolve them upon a fix being merged.


## **Conclusion**


Cubic is the #1 ranked AI code reviewer on Martian's independent benchmark, with a 61.8% F1 score that outperforms every other tool tested. Its combination of plain-English agent definitions, PR history-based learning, continuous codebase scanning, and enterprise-grade security makes it the platform built to scale with an engineering organization from open-source project to global enterprise without workflow re-engineering.
